findings.description: SHEET-MAP-002's plain text — 'key mark read-back by row identity (symbol), asserting one row per symbol and erroring loudly if violated' — reads as a property of the read-back operation itself. All three A-direction sketches converge on exactly that: a standalone function taking the actual read-back rows (MarkRow/PricePass-shaped data) and asserting symbol-uniqueness over THAT data, erroring via typed Result::Err (A1/A2/A3 all reason this is the only way to protect against 'externally-sourced sheet state' being silently corrupted — A1 assumption 3, A3 assumption 2). The real code does not do this. The ONLY duplicate-symbol guard in the crate lives in render_positions, checked over Snapshot.positions (the kernel-side WRITE path that establishes row identity before publish) — not over anything read back from the sheet. Per the code's own comments and the dedicated test (duplicate_symbol_guard_is_defensive_and_one_row_per_symbol_holds), this guard is 'structurally UNREACHABLE through the real API' because Snapshot.positions is typed Map<Symbol,_>, so it can never actually fire. Meanwhile the true read-back path — read_marks, operating on symbols: &[Symbol] and the client-returned PricePass: BTreeMap<Symbol, PriceReading> — performs ZERO duplicate detection: any duplicate symbol reading (e.g. from a stale/manually-edited/corrupted live sheet — the exact externally-sourced-state risk the requirement is guarding against) would simply be silently overwritten by BTreeMap::insert's last-write-wins semantics, never an error, let alone a loud one. So the code's 'erroring loudly if violated' contract is dead code sitting at the wrong pipeline stage (protecting against an impossible internal-typing scenario) while the actual read-back stage the requirement names has no protection at all. All three B-direction reconstructions independently surface this same asymmetry from the code: B1's SHEET-POS-KEY-3 and SHEET-MARK-KEY-1, B2's explicit 'the settle pass does not itself re-check for duplicates; it relies on the render-time guarantee,' and B3's SHEET-POS-DEFENSIVE + SHEET-MARK-KEY all locate the enforceable check on the render/write side and note the read-back/settle side has no independent check of its own.

Code-side surplus: ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow's Display implementation is pinned (by test, and identically reconstructed by B1/B2/B3) to render as its derived Debug form verbatim — e.g. exactly `DuplicateSymbolRow("AMZN")` — with no separate human-readable message. SHEET-MAP-002's 'erroring loudly' says nothing about error-text shape; this exact-format contract is a real, test-enforced constant the spec text never states.

Code-side surplus: row/read-back key ordering is BTreeMap<Symbol,_>-derived ascending-symbol order (B2 states this explicitly; B1/B3 imply it via the BTreeMap/BTreeSet typing throughout Positions rendering and the marks maps). SHEET-MAP-002 speaks only to uniqueness and loud-erroring, never to ordering — an unstated but code-pinned detail.

Low-stability, non-unanimous: A2 alone adds a distinct MissingSymbol error variant rejecting empty/whitespace-only symbols as invalid rows; A1 and A3 do not include this case, and A2 itself flags it as 'not explicit in the EARS.' Since it doesn't survive across A-runs and isn't spec-traced, this is an individual-run assumption artifact, not a cross-run finding — noted only for completeness, not counted toward the classification.

notes: Read both target files in full (lib.rs, tests/mapping.rs) before classifying. Core mechanism confirmed by direct code inspection: render_positions (lib.rs lines ~540-545) holds the only Err(ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow) branch, explicitly commented as defensively guarding a structurally-unreachable case given Snapshot.positions: Map<Symbol,_>; read_marks (lines ~817-887) takes symbols: &[Symbol] and PricePass: BTreeMap<Symbol,PriceReading> with no uniqueness check anywhere in its body — duplicates would silently collapse via BTreeMap::insert. Tests in mapping.rs confirm only the happy path (sort+dedup length check) and the Display-format contract via a manually-constructed error value (ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow("AMZN".to_string())), never exercising the duplicate branch through the real API — consistent with all three B reconstructions' explicit 'defensive/unreachable, not exercised' framing. This is a strong, well-observed, high-agreement BD-DRIFT rather than a borderline call: both directions independently triangulate on the same structural gap (enforcement point vs. requirement's named operation) from opposite starting points (spec-forced invention vs. code-read reconstruction).
